newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco, Belgium to boost ties against drug dealers.
newsitem.headline: Morocco, Belgium to boost ties against drug dealers.

text.p: Morocco and Belgium agreed on Monday to strengthen cooperation in the fight to eradicate drug trafficking, organised crime and clandestine immigration, the official MAP news agency said.
Visiting Interior Minister Johan Vande Lanotte held talks with Moroccan officials in Rabat on "ways to eradicate drug trafficking and organised crime," MAP said.
Rabat and Brussels, which have already initialled an agreement to fight drugs and criminality, are expected to sign a convention soon including the clandestine immigration issue, MAP said.
MAP said the Belgian government was ready to grant Morocco substantial funds to help it fight drug smuggling. It gave no other details.

To improve its image abroad, Morocco recently drew up a draft law that will raise the penalty for drug trafficking to up to 30 years in jail and fines to up to 800,000 dirhams ($86,000), the Interior Ministry said.

Officials say Morocco's northern Rif mountainous province has more than 60,000 hectares (150,000 acres) given over to cannabis cultivation, of which large quantities are annually transformed into a cannabis resin and exported to Europe.

"Morocco's struggle against drug trafficking is also based on international cooperation (needed) because of the tight links between drug smuggling, money laundering, crime and terrorism...international solidarity is necessary to eradicate this curse," the ministry said earlier.

The country has signed several agreements with European Union countries aimed at attracting up to $1.0 billion investment per year to develop the poor northern area, replace cannabis cultivation with legal crops, and discourage illegal immigration to Europe.

Last year, Moroccan security forces seized 103 tonnes of cannabis bound for Europe, including Belgium. More than 18,000 drug traffickers were arrested, including 342 foreigners, mostly Europeans, the ministry added.
